page: Microsoft Azure F64als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Falsv7 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. The server provides 64 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores with a single thread per core, ensuring dedicated compute resources without hyperthreading overhead. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the F64als_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests. This processing power is supported by high memory bandwidth, reaching 410.03 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 205.23 GB/sec for large-block write operations. The CPU features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography extensions, which contribute to its top-tier PassMark CPU score of 116,710.13 and strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression. Additionally, the server achieves 171.03 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and displays strong LLM inference capabilities, processing 316.09 tokens per second for medium 7B models.

The F64als_v7 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints, maximizing raw CPU performance per resource unit. However, the 2.0 GB of RAM per core represents a clear tradeoff, making this server less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory data processing. The lack of local storage also requires external storage attachment. This configuration is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as high-throughput web serving, batch processing, CPU-based machine learning inference, and cryptography tasks.
